data.narrative:
Pasqal is a pre-IPO quantum computing company founded by Alain Aspect and four co-founders, having raised €340M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises a small but growing peer universe of 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 6 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable to Pasqal due to insufficient comparable data. Despite six same-sector peers existing, none meet the filtering criteria for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers—the minimum threshold of three datapoints required for robust median calculation was not met. A broad all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and misrepresent the specific dynamics of quantum computing valuations at the pre-IPO stage.

Given the constrained comp universe and absence of directly comparable pre-IPO quantum firms with sufficient datapoint density, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range using standard VC methods. The sector remains early-stage with minimal public trading history and dispersed funding rounds at varying scales. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue benchmarks across the peer set, wide heterogeneity in technical approaches and commercialization timelines, and limited precedent for quantum computing exits at this maturity level. A defensible valuation would require either expansion of stage-specific private comp data or explicit reliance on cost-of-capital or scenario-based approaches outside the peer-set framework.
